strings.name: Patrick Modiano
strings.summary: Born near Paris, Modiano turned to writing with encouragement from Raymond Queneau. Through searches for people, disappearances and city streets, he explores memory and identity and the shadows of occupied France. He debuted in 1968, won the 1978 Goncourt for Missing Person and the 2014 Nobel Prize. Dora Bruder combines investigation, personal memory and the fate of a Holocaust victim; his writing also extends to film scripts.
